findings.what: Direct source registration can follow an existing in-case symlink and overwrite another case artifact.
findings.why: register_local_source resumes and validates only registered documents, then _under_root resolves the destination alias and accepts it when the target remains inside the case. The new-source branch writes bytes to that resolved target. A shared case can place data/raw/new-id/payload.csv as a symlink to case.json and cause the CSV payload to replace case.json; no whole-tree scan runs on this public path.

findings.what: The dispatcher scans the case only once before a multi-owner loop, so a dynamic owner can introduce a link that later phases follow.
findings.why: P5 and P6 invoke external reasoning code with the live case_root. After that code returns, the loop calls load_snapshot and subsequent owners without another _scan_case_tree. A link introduced between phases can therefore redirect state, replay, review, receipt, or report reads and writes outside their intended artifact boundary during the same public invocation.

findings.what: A completed snapshot with missing artifact identities is trusted as complete.
findings.why: load_snapshot converts a missing or non-mapping identities field to an empty mapping, and changed_identities checks only keys that are present. A shared case can provide sequential P0-P7 completed entries, status complete, and no identities; resolve_workflow then returns terminal completion without hashing any required source, prepared data, detector plan, gate receipt, draft, replay, review, or Gate B artifact.

findings.what: Canonical-equivalent Unicode identities bypass Gate A, reviewer, and Gate B role separation.
findings.why: Both independence checks compare casefold values while _required_identity only strips whitespace. Composed and decomposed forms such as Café and Café remain unequal under casefold alone even though canonical_key treats them as the same identity, allowing one logical person to occupy supposedly independent roles.

findings.what: Future Gate A and Gate B decisions are retained across the resolver loop and consumed without a fresh human turn.
findings.why: normalize_inputs captures all supplied decisions before execution, and the same mapping is reused after every newly completed phase. A gate_a decision supplied before P3 or gate_b supplied before P6 can become immediately actionable once the preceding phase seals, bypassing the required informed pause at each human gate.

findings.what: Attempt failures persist common credentials because the central error sanitizer recognizes only three token prefixes.
findings.why: safe_error feeds failure.json, events.jsonl, state.failures, and blocked_reason, but _SECRET covers only sk_live_, ghp_, and github_pat_. Dynamic-owner exceptions containing Authorization: Bearer values, password or token assignments, AWS keys, Slack tokens, or credential-bearing URLs are stored verbatim across retries even though review.py already has broader redaction patterns.

findings.what: A failed multi-source P1 attempt partially commits earlier sources instead of preserving atomic attempt semantics.
findings.why: _register_sources calls register_local_source directly for each request, and each call mutates live raw bytes, receipts, and sources.json. If a later request is invalid, run_attempts records failure and retries but never rolls back the earlier successful registrations, leaving durable source mutation under an unavailable P1 outcome.

findings.what: README projection can delete journalist-authored Markdown that happens to equal the legacy Outputs block.
findings.why: After bounded marker removal, project_readme performs a global exact-string replacement of _OUTPUTS. An unmarked journalist section with the same heading and links is removed during completion or invalidation projection, violating the explicit preservation requirement and causing reachable authored-content loss.

evidence.output: The deterministic scan processed 7 files with zero regex findings and emitted PASS, but its ledger marked 10 of 12 scanner categories not_covered. Manual boundary analysis below supplies the missing reachability coverage rather than treating PASS as the audit verdict.

evidence.command: read task.md and task.json gate evidence
evidence.output: Task 27 explicitly requires whole-case validation on every public resume/read/write path, strict human turn boundaries, identity/invalidation integrity, inert Markdown, journalist README preservation, atomic attempts, and audit of case containment, source mutation, detector execution, and report serialization. The supplied clean gate is 711/711 passing at the audited hash.

inspect_case and resume_case do not scan the tree; _under_root resolves aliases and accepts targets that remain under the root. register_local_source enters through resume_case and its new-source branch writes directly to the resolved destination, confirming the in-case alias overwrite path.

Dynamic loader identities map only to fixed installed skill/persona paths and unknown owners are rejected, so case-selected code loading is not reachable. However, run_workflow scans only before the loop, gives dynamic invocations the live case root, never rescans between owners, and reuses all initially supplied gate inputs across fresh resolutions.

The identity phase map covers P1-P7 artifacts, but comparison iterates only recorded identities and state loading validates only that state is a dict. Missing identities therefore produce no invalidation before a sequential P7 completed map is honored.

Role separation uses casefold-only comparisons while the project's canonical_key normalizes NFC after case folding and portable identity validation rejects non-normalized/control-bearing components. The stronger canonical policy is not applied to reviewer or journalist identities.

The narrow state sanitizer is applied before writing failure.json, event records, failures, and blocked_reason. The report boundary independently handles sensitive keys, assignment forms, Bearer values, Slack/AWS/provider prefixes, demonstrating that common credentials missed by state.py are expected inputs.

P1 loops over requests and each registration commits live source bytes, its receipt, and sources.json before the next request is validated. attempt_dir is not used by this handler, so a later failure has no transactional rollback.

Detector metadata and query paths come from fixed installed packages; YAML uses safe_load or a restricted literal parser; detector/table identifiers are constrained; SQL is SELECT-only, parameterized, and rejects external readers; DuckDB is read-only with external access disabled; execution limits are positive integers; owned paths reject aliases. No command execution, unsafe deserialization, SQL injection, network transport, or weak crypto exploit was found in this boundary.

Dataset claim IDs and statements are HTML-escaped, Markdown metacharacters are escaped, and HTTP(S) colons are neutralized, so dataset-derived XSS and bare autolinks are not reachable. Separately, README projection globally deletes every exact legacy Outputs block, including journalist-authored content.

evidence.command: read scanner dependency and permissions sections plus implement-return.json
evidence.output: The scan reported no dependency vulnerability and no insecure-permission hit; the implementation file list changes no dependency manifest. Changed runtime paths perform no outbound TLS/network activity, shell command execution, eval/exec, pickle loading, or permissive chmod.
